title: AI-Augmented Fraud Detection in Cloud Platforms: GRA-Based Risk Ranking with Cybersecurity and Threat Prevention for SAP HANA Healthcare ERP
venue: International Journal of Advanced Research in Computer Science & Technology (IJARCST)
tldr: A DevOps-centric AI pipeline combining supervised classification with Grey Relational Analysis achieves 88-90% recall and reduces false positives by 15-20% for cloud-based fraud detection.
problem_and_motivation: Traditional fraud detection systems relying on rule-based engines struggle with zero-day and multi-entity fraud rings while generating high false positives. Existing systems lack integration with modern DevOps workflows, making frequent retraining and redeployment difficult. Few works fully integrate DevOps-centric CI/CD pipelines with graph-based risk scoring for production-grade fraud detection at petabyte scale.
approach: DevOps-centric AI analytics pipeline using Azure DevOps and GitHub for automated data ingestion, model training, validation, and deployment.
Graph-Risk-Adaptive (GRA) ranking module analyzes entity graphs (accounts, users, devices, transactions) for relational risk scoring.
Hybrid approach combining supervised classifier for known fraud patterns with GRA module for structural fraud detection.
Synthetic data simulation mimicking real-world operation volumes with normal and fraudulent behaviors including fraud rings.
Distributed data ingestion using Kafka streaming engine with Spark-based preprocessing and feature extraction.
Feedback loops with CI/CD pipelines enabling continuous model retraining and adaptation to concept drift.
Evaluation benchmarking detection effectiveness, latency, scalability, and adaptability across three system variants.
findings: num: Hybrid model achieves 88-90% recall, 89-91% precision, and 89-90% F1-scores compared to baseline 81% recall.
num: Detection of structured fraud rings improves by 30-35% relative to baseline supervised model.
num: False-positive rates decrease by 15-20% when using GRA ranking compared to anomaly-detector-enhanced variant.
num: Pipeline sustains throughput of 5,000 TPS with end-to-end latency under 1 second.
num: Graph computations add 150-250ms overhead compared to classification-only path.
num: System reclaims 90-95% of previous performance within one retraining cycle after concept drift injection.
Graph-based features contribute 40-50% of incremental detection power beyond behavioral features.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper contributes a unified DevOps-centric AI analytics pipeline that integrates cloud-native infrastructure with graph-based risk scoring for large-scale fraud detection. It introduces the GRA ranking module that captures relational and structural fraud patterns often missed by traditional classifiers. The work demonstrates the value of combining CI/CD pipelines with continuous model adaptation to handle concept drift in fraud detection. The framework provides a scalable, adaptive approach aligning with the demands of cloud-native, petabyte-scale transactional environments.

topic_relevance.topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: All topic domains were systematically scanned. Domain 6 (Predictive Modeling) flagged 6.A as high for the DevOps-centric predictive pipeline. Domain 8 (Anomaly Detection) flagged 8.A as high for core fraud detection focus and 8.B as high for the GRA-based algorithms developed. Domain 10 (Privacy) flagged 10.A as medium for cloud security mechanisms. Domains 1-5, 7, 9, 11-14 were considered and rejected as the paper does not address Filipino demographics, expense categorization, budgeting strategies, mobile design, engagement, evaluation frameworks (beyond fraud metrics), savings, debt management, or ML deployment beyond DevOps pipelines. The paper's topical coverage centers on predictive modeling and anomaly detection algorithms for cloud-based fraud detection with emphasis on graph analytics and continuous adaptation.
